'''''Simonettoia''''' is an [[extinct]] genus of [[archosauromorph]] reptile in the family [[Tanystropheidae]], known from the [[Late Triassic]] ([[Norian]] age) [[Forni Dolostone]] of Italy. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Simonettoia tilaventina''''', known from a partial articulated skeleton. It is most similar to the contemporary ''[[Langobardisaurus]]'', but differs from it in the vertebral structure and limb proportions.

== Discovery and naming ==
[[File:Dolomia di Forni tanystropheid localities.png|thumb|left|''S. tilaventina'' [[Type locality (biology)|type locality]] (3) in the Forni Dolostone]]
The ''Simonettoia'' fossil material was discovered by R. Rigo at some point prior to 2006 in outcrops of the [[Forni Dolostone]] near the confluence of the Forchiar Brook with the [[Tagliamento River]]. This site is located near the town of [[Villa Santina]] in [[Province of Udine|Udine Province]], northeastern Italy. The specimen is housed in the Museo Friulano di Storia Naturale (MFSN) in Udine, where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen MFSN 24992. It consists of a partial, neatly articulated skeleton, preserved on a [[Compression fossil|slab and counterslab]] of [[dolostone]]. Most of the skeleton is visible in [[Anatomical terms of location#Dorsal and ventral|dorsal]] (top) view. Much of the vertebral column (neck, trunk, and tail), ribs, left forelimb and hindlimb, pelvis, and pectoral girdle are exposed. The skull, right limbs, and at least the ends of the neck and tail are not visible; they may be contained within the block, but the fragile nature of the bones prevented further [[Fossil preparation|preparation]], and the similar bone–rock density precluded investigation via [[CT scan]]ning.<ref name="Simonettoia" /> The specimen was briefly mentioned in four reports beginning in 2006, where it was referred to as a juvenile specimen of ''[[Langobardisaurus]]'', another tanystropheid known from the Forni Dolostone.<ref name="DV2012" />

In 2026, Silvio Renesto and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Simonettoia tilaventina'' as a new genus and species of tanystropheid based on these fossil remains, designating MFSN 24992 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Simonettoia'', honors Luca Simonetto, a MFSN employee who died about three years prior.<ref name="SDS38" /> The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''tilaventina'', is derived from the {{lang|la|Tilaventus}}, the [[Latin]] name for the Tagliamento, near where the only known specimen was found.<ref name="Simonettoia" />
